title: Quota-aware user cohort routing with negotiated fallback budgets
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Free, paid, and enterprise customers share endpoints. During multi-region spikes we must avoid hard failures for free-tier samples while preserving enterprise SLOs. Current tier demotion is coarse: requests are dropped or bluntly redirected, causing noisy errors and unclear billing implications.

Goal: Implement a quota-aware routing layer that: 1) routes incoming requests by tier with regional affinity, 2) maintains negotiated fallback budgets per cohort (free/paid/enterprise) so requests can be soft-degraded instead of dropped, and 3) exposes clear metrics and audit logs for billing/corrections. The mechanism should be pluggable into the admission-controller and compatible with Canary/Beta rollouts in Redwood Console.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Admission controller enforces per-cohort soft budgets such that at least 95% of paid and enterprise requests meet latency SLOs under simulated 2x baseline traffic while free cohort receives degraded (lower-cost model) responses rather than failures.
2) Regional affinity maintained: >90% of requests from a region are served in-region unless capacity exceeded and fallback rules trigger.
3) All demotion/fallback events are logged to audit-stream with tenant, cohort, reason, from_model, to_model, and amount charged.
4) Console dashboard shows real-time cohort budgets, usage, and demotion counts.
5) Rollout plan includes canary on 5% traffic and automatic rollback on demotion spike >300/min.
technical_design:
High-level: Add a CohortBudget module to the admission-controller (go service) that maintains an in-memory leaky-bucket per (tenant-cohort-region) backed by a durable store for cross-instance reconciliation (Redis with compare-and-swap). Each bucket has: negotiated_budget_tokens (monthly allotment normalized to token units), emergency_allowance (fraction, configurable per plan), and decay_windows for burst smoothing.

Routing decision path:
- Lookup tenant -> cohort -> region affinity.
- Evaluate primary model capacity and predicted latency.
- Check CohortBudget.available(request_cost). If available: admit to preferred lane.
- If not available but emergency_allowance > 0: admit to fallback lane (lower-cost quantized model or constrained tokens) and decrement emergency_allowance. Mark as 'soft-demoted'.
- If emergency_allowance exhausted: if enterprise and cross-region capacity exists, spill to remote region variant; otherwise reject with 429 and structured JSON explaining quota status.

Features: negotiated budgets can be overridden via billing tags for one-off events (support/invoice adjustments). CohortBudget exposes atomic reservation APIs to avoid double-spend across admission-controller replicas. Auditing middleware emits a demotion record to the event pipeline.

Implementation notes: use a sharded Redis keyspace per region to reduce cross-region latency. For scale tests, simulate 10k tenants with mixed cohorts and verify median admission latency adds <4ms overhead. Include unit tests for race conditions and e2e smoke with the runtime serving simulator.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag gated rollout in admission-controller binary.
2) Canary: enable for internal tenants + 5% of paid customers in us-west only. Monitor: demotion_count, latency_slo_violations, error_rate, billing_docs mismatch.
3) Expand to paid + 10% free in eu-west.
4) Full enablement with per-tenant opt-outs and billing reconciliation job.
5) Post-rollout: 2-week monitoring window and adjust emergency_allowance defaults based on observed demand curves.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for atomic reservation, backpressure logic, and emergency allowance decrement.
- Load test: synthetic client with region skew to simulate a regional outage and 3x traffic spike; assert cohort-level SLOs.
- Soak test for 72 hours with mixed bursts to validate long-tail fairness.
- Integration test with Console dashboard and audit-stream consumer to validate visibility and billing tags.
- Chaos test: kill Redis shard and validate admission-controller gracefully falls back to local best-effort heuristics and emits degraded-mode warning.
metrics_and_observability: Expose: cohort_budget_remaining, cohort_emergency_allowance, demotion_count_by_tier, demotion_rate_per_min, admission_latency_added_ms, cross_region_spill_count. Dashboards: per-region cohort heatmap; alert if demotion_rate_paid > 1% sustained for 10m. Audit logs: demotion events to kafka topic 'admissions.demotions'.
open_questions:
1) How should negotiated budgets map to billing units for embeddings vs generation? (finance input required)
2) Should enterprise customers have negative emergency_allowance (i.e., borrow from next billing period) or simply higher spill-to-remote privileges?
3) Do legal/compliance teams require disclosure of soft-demotions in SLA docs?
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Over-eager demotion for paid customers harming perceived quality. Mitigation: conservative defaults for paid tier and canary throttle.
Risk: Redis CAS contention under hot keys. Mitigation: shard keys and local fast-path caching with short TTLs.
Risk: Billing discrepancies due to demotions. Mitigation: log canonical demotion records and implement offline reconciliation job with idempotent corrections.
next_steps:
1) Spike: implement CohortBudget prototype (Rafael) and demo with runtime simulator by 2026-03-12.
2) Product: confirm mapping to billing units and emergency_allowance defaults (PM sync scheduled).
3) Design: small Console widgets for cohort budget visualization (DES task).
4) Schedule security review if audit schema includes tenant-sensitive fields.
